mainTopic: מסייע אין בו ממש; whether two partners need one שיעור or two; and the משנה about a vessel being secondary (טפל) to its contents
overview: This amud has three parts. First, the גמרא brings three sources to prove that a helper (מסייע) has no legal weight: רבי יוסי's horse and donkey, רבי אליעזר's כהן standing partly on a vessel, and the left hand helping the right in קבלת הדם. It concludes 'שמע מינה'. Next, it returns to רבי מאיר's ruling that when each of two people could do a מלאכה alone, both are חייב. It asks whether each person needs his own full שיעור or whether one שיעור covers both, and רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree. Three proofs (the זב on a bed, the deer, and partners who stole and slaughtered) support 'one שיעור for all'. רב אשי's fourth proof, from a weaver's reed, is rejected, and רב נחמן corrects a reversed version of that ברייתא. Then a new משנה teaches that a vessel or bed is secondary to what it holds, and that carrying a corpse or impure items makes one liable, while רבי שמעון exempts. The גמרא begins discussing when the vessel itself creates liability, and רב ששת's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Horse and donkey: only the main legs count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that a זב riding a horse makes a garment טמא only through its front legs, and on a donkey only through its hind legs. The גמרא infers that the weaker legs are just helpers, and a helper does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A horse makes a garment טמא through its front legs, and a donkey through its hind legs, because a horse leans on its front legs and a donkey on its hind legs. But why should the other legs not count? They help hold the animal up too! It must be because we say that a helper has no real substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה and uses it as a proof that a helper (מסייע) does not count legally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garment under the horse's hind legs still carries some of the weight, yet רבי יוסי says it stays טהור. The only reason that makes sense is that those legs merely help the main legs. A helper is legally nothing, so מסייע אין בו ממש.

keyTerms.meaning: A helper, one who assists the main actor
Has no substance, does not count legally
Leaning or main support
Its front legs (literally 'its hands')
But why? Used to set up an inference

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle (מסייע אין בו ממש) is the basis for understanding the earlier cases on the דף about two people doing a מלאכה together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
The horse renders impure through its front legs,
phrases.notes: This is talking about a זב riding the horse, with a garment lying underneath it.

phrases.english: the donkey — through its hind legs,
because the horse leans on its front legs,
and the donkey on its hind legs.
But why?
Don't the legs assist each other!
Is it not because we say
one who assists has no substance?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? הָא קָא מְסַיַּיע בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי! לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן מְסַיֵּיעַ אֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the דף's earlier question of whether a מסייע has legal substance
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה of רבי יוסי about a זב riding a horse or donkey

steps.title: כהן standing with one foot on a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings רבי אליעזר's ruling: a כהן with one foot on a vessel or stone serves validly if he could stand on the floor foot alone. This shows the foot on the vessel is only a helper.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We also learned this. רבי אליעזר says: If one foot was on a vessel and one on the floor, or one foot on a stone and one on the floor, we check. If he could stand on one foot with the vessel or stone taken away, his עבודה is valid. If not, his עבודה is invalid. But why is it valid? The feet help each other! It must be because a helper has no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a second proof that a helper does not count, from the laws of עבודה in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן must stand directly on the floor of the עזרה while serving, with nothing in between. If the floor foot can hold him alone, the foot on the vessel is only helping, so it is ignored and the עבודה is valid. If the vessel foot is truly needed, it is a real support, and the עבודה is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it, meaning there is support from a משנה or ברייתא
The floor of the עזרה
His Temple service is valid
His Temple service is invalid
We look and evaluate

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We, too, have also learned it.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
one of his feet on the vessel
and one of his feet on the floor,
one of his feet on the stone
and one of his feet on the floor —
we see: whenever, if the vessel were removed
or the stone were removed,
he could stand on one foot —
his service is valid;
and if not — his service is invalid.
But why?
Don't the feet assist each other!
Is it not because we say
one who assists has no substance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent proof for the same principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's ruling about a כהן standing partly on a vessel or stone

steps.title: Receiving blood with the right hand while the left helps
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings the rule that if a כהן received the blood with his right hand and his left hand helped, the עבודה is valid. This shows the helping hand does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We also learned this. If he received the blood with his right hand and his left hand helped, his עבודה is valid. But why? The hands help each other! It must be because a helper has no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a third proof that a helper does not count, from קבלת הדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה must be done with the right hand, and the left hand would normally make it פסול. Even so, when the left hand only helps, the עבודה stays valid. So the left hand is a mere מסייע and is legally ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: Received, here meaning received the blood of a קרבן (קבלת הדם)
Right hand, required for עבודה
Left hand

phrases.english: Ravina said:
We, too, have also learned it.
If he received the blood with the right hand,
and the left hand assists it —
his service is valid.
But why?
Don't the hands assist each other!
Is it not because we say
one who assists has no substance?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof for the same principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule about receiving blood with the right hand while the left assists

steps.title: Conclusion: a helper has no substance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proofs and concludes that מסייע אין בו ממש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the first topic by accepting that a helper has no legal substance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שמע מינה' tells us the proof is accepted with no rejection. The question of whether a מסייע counts is now settled: it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, meaning the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: מסייע אין בו ממש: when one part does the main work and another only helps, the helper is legally ignored. This is proven from the horse and donkey, the כהן's feet, and the כהן's hands.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 3 and closes the topic

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר: both capable, both liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the ברייתא that when each of two people could do the מלאכה alone, רבי מאיר holds both are חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If this one could do it alone and that one could do it alone, רבי מאיר holds them liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back an earlier line from the ברייתא. It is setting up a new question about this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a setup line and does not decide anything new. It reminds us that, according to רבי מאיר, two people who each could do the act alone are both חייב when they do it together. The next step asks what this requires.

keyTerms.meaning: This one is able and that one is able, meaning each could do the act alone
Holds liable

phrases.english: The Master said:
If this one is capable and that one is capable,
Rabbi Meir deems them liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: זֶה יָכוֹל וְזֶה יָכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a new topic by re-quoting the earlier ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: if each could do it alone, both are חייב

steps.title: Separate measure for each, or one measure for all?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask whether, for both to be חייב, each person needs his own full שיעור or whether one שיעור is enough for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Do we need a full amount for this one and a full amount for that one, or perhaps one amount is enough for all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question about how much two partners must do in order to both be חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For example, if two people together carry out a fig's worth of food, is each חייב, or does each one need his own fig's worth? The question is whether the שיעור is counted per person or for the act as a whole.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them, introducing a question that was in doubt
The minimum amount needed for liability
Or perhaps
For all of them

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Do we require a measure for this one and a measure for that one,
or perhaps one measure for them all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the details of רבי מאיר's ruling quoted in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether each partner needs his own full שיעור, or one shared שיעור covers both

steps.title: רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree. One requires a שיעור for each person, and the other says one שיעור covers everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רב המנונא: one said a full amount is needed for each person, and one said one amount is enough for all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that two אמוראים argued about this exact question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of the question have a supporter, and the גמרא does not say which אמורא held which view. The next steps bring proofs for the view of one שיעור for all.

keyTerms.meaning: One said, used when the גמרא does not say which אמורא held which view

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda and Rav Hamnuna disagreed:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר שִׁיעוּר לָזֶה וְשִׁיעוּר לָזֶה,
phrases.english: One said: a measure for this one and a measure for that one,
and one said: one measure for them all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the question in step 6 was argued by אמוראים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: either a separate שיעור for each person, or one שיעור for all

steps.title: זב on a bed over four garments
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא in the name of רבא proves 'one שיעור for all' from a זב sitting on a bed with a garment under each leg. All four garments become טמא, even though only one זב's weight is spread among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: We also learned this. If a זב was sitting on a bed with four garments under its four legs, they are all טמא, because the bed cannot stand on three legs. But why? We should need a full זב's weight for this garment and a full זב's weight for that one! It must be because we say one שיעור is enough for all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a first proof that one shared שיעור is enough for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each leg carries only a quarter of the זב's weight, yet every garment becomes טמא by מדרס. Since the bed needs all four legs to stand, each leg is a real supporter, not a mere helper. One full זב's weight is enough to make all of them טמא, which matches 'one שיעור for all'.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
Garments or cloths
The state of being a זב; here, a full זב's weight as the impurity measure
It should require

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
We, too, have also learned it:
If a zav was sitting on a bed
and four garments were
under the four legs of the bed — they are impure,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד עַל שָׁלֹשׁ.
phrases.english: because it cannot stand on three.
But why?
Let it require a zav's measure for this one
and a zav's measure for that one!
Is it not because we say
one measure for them all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof for one side of the מחלוקת in step 7
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in זבים about a זב on a bed with four garments under its legs

steps.title: Two people trapping a deer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves 'one שיעור for all' from the deer case. When one person could not lock the door alone and two locked it, both are חייב for צידה, even though there was only one trapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this. If a deer entered a house and one person locked the door before it, he is liable. If two locked it, they are exempt. If one could not lock it alone and two locked it, they are liable. But why? We should need a full trapping for this one and a full trapping for that one! It must be because we say one שיעור is enough for all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof for 'one שיעור for all', from the מלאכה of צידה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last case, the two together performed only one act of trapping, yet both are חייב. This shows that one complete act can make each partner fully liable. The proof comes from the case where neither could do it alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A deer
Locked the door
Trapping, one of the ל״ט מלאכות
Exempt
Liable

steps.confusionAlert: Do not be confused by the middle case, where two locked the door and are exempt. That case is where each could have done it alone (זה יכול וזה יכול), following the view that exempts them. The proof comes only from the last case, where neither could lock it alone and both are חייב.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
We, too, have also learned it:
A deer that entered the house,
and one person locked the door before it — he is liable.
If two locked it — they are exempt.
If one could not lock it alone,
and two locked it — they are liable.
But why?
Let it require a measure of trapping for this one
and a measure of trapping for that one!
Is it not because we say
one measure for them all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proof for the same side as step 8
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה about two people trapping a deer on שבת

steps.title: Partners who stole and slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: רבינא proves 'one שיעור for all' from partners who stole an animal and slaughtered it together. Both must pay the קנס of ארבעה וחמשה even though there was only one שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We also learned this. Partners who stole and slaughtered are liable. But why? We should need a full slaughtering for this one and a full slaughtering for that one! It must be because we say one שיעור is enough for all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a third proof for 'one שיעור for all', from the laws of a thief who slaughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנס of ארבעה וחמשה applies to a thief who slaughters the stolen animal. Here two partners did only one שחיטה together, yet both are חייב. One complete act counts fully for each of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Partners
They stole
They slaughtered
Slaughtering, which triggers the payment of ארבעה וחמשה

steps.whatToRemember: The סוגיא has three proofs (the bed of a זב, the deer, and the partners who slaughtered) for the view that when two people do one act together, one שיעור is enough to make both חייב.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
We, too, have also learned it:
Partners who stole and slaughtered — are liable.
But why?
Let it require a measure of slaughtering for this one
and a measure of slaughtering for that one!
Is it not because we say
one measure for them all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof for the same side as steps 8 and 9
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה about partners who stole and slaughtered (ארבעה וחמשה)

steps.title: רב אשי brings a proof from two people carrying a weaver's reed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says a ברייתא supports 'one שיעור for all': two people who carried out a weaver's reed are liable, even though there is only one reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said: We also learned this. Two people who carried out a weaver's reed are liable. Why? Each one should need his own full amount of carrying! Isn't it because we say one שיעור counts for everyone?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a fourth proof that one שיעור is enough for two people, this time from a ברייתא about carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people carried one reed, and both are liable. If each person needed his own full amount, the reed would have to be big enough for two. Since the ברייתא simply says both are liable, it seems one amount covers both.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned it (in a ברייתא or משנה): a formula that introduces support from a teaching of the תנאים
A weaver's reed, a rod used in weaving
The minimum amount that makes one liable for carrying out
One minimum amount counts for everyone involved

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said:
We too have also learned it:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ קָנֶה שֶׁל גַּרְדִּי — חַיָּיבִין.
phrases.english: Two who carried out a weaver's reed are liable.
And why?
Let it require a carrying-measure for this one
and a carrying-measure for that one!
Is it not because we say
one measure for all of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth proof after those of רב פפא, רב נחמן בר יצחק, and רבינא.
steps.raayaObject: The view that one שיעור covers all participants
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: two who carried out a weaver's reed are liable

steps.title: Maybe the reed was big enough for two cooking amounts
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא answers that perhaps the reed was big enough to cook a light egg for each person, so each one had a full שיעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרבא said to רב אשי: Maybe the reed had enough wood to cook a light egg for this one and a light egg for that one!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא rejects רב אשי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount for carrying wood is enough to cook a light egg. If the reed was large enough to make two such amounts, then each person carried a full amount of his own. So the ברייתא could also fit the view that each person needs his own שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps: a typical opening for pushing away a proof
Enough wood to cook a light, easily cooked egg. This is the שיעור for carrying wood.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
Perhaps it has in it
enough to cook a light egg for this one
and a light egg for that one!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִילְמָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב אשי's proof. The view that one שיעור covers all is not disproved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be about a large reed that contains a full שיעור for each person.

steps.title: Why mention a weaver's reed in particular?
steps.stepSummary: The proof is defended: if the point were about firewood size, the ברייתא would have said any reed. Naming a weaver's reed shows it is a single tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it teach us about an ordinary reed. Why mention a weaver's reed specifically?
steps.whatsHappening: The proof is defended against רב אחא's rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the liability were based on how much firewood is in the reed, any reed would do. The ברייתא chose a weaver's reed, which matters as one whole tool. That suggests the ברייתא means a single unit with one שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem that follows from the other side's claim
What is different? Why this case specifically?
Ordinary, of the general world

phrases.english: If so, let it teach us an ordinary reed;
what is different about a weaver's?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לַישְׁמְעִינַן קָנֶה דְעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the rejection in step 12 to save the proof of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the wording: the specific choice of a weaver's reed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reed is just firewood measured for egg-cooking.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reed is treated as a weaving tool, one unit.

steps.title: Maybe the reed was big enough to weave two cloths
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected again: perhaps the weaver's reed was big enough to weave a cloth for each person, so each still had his own שיעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it had enough to weave a cloth for this one and enough to weave a cloth for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The defense from step 13 is answered, and the proof is pushed away once more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fine, it is a weaving tool. But the שיעור for a weaving tool is enough to weave a cloth. A long reed could be enough for two cloths, giving each person a full amount.

keyTerms.meaning: To weave a cloth: the שיעור for a weaving tool

phrases.english: And perhaps it has in it
enough to weave a cloth for this one
and enough to weave a cloth for that one,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ כְּדֵי לֶאֱרוֹג מַפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense given in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the weaver's reed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even as a weaving tool, the reed could hold a full weaving-שיעור for each person.

steps.title: No proof can be brought from this ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion: the weaver's reed ברייתא does not prove the question either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, nothing can be learned from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion of רב אשי's proof by declaring it inconclusive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא can be read as a large reed, it fits both views. The earlier proofs, from the זב, the deer, and the partners, are not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: Nothing can be learned from it

steps.confusionAlert: Only רב אשי's proof fails here. The idea that one שיעור covers all is not rejected.

phrases.english: Rather, from this there is nothing to learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵהָא לֵיכָּא לְמִשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the rejection in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The weaver's reed ברייתא is not a proof for 'one שיעור for all'.

steps.title: A תנא recites the reed ברייתא with the opinions reversed
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites before רב נחמן that two who carried a weaver's reed are exempt, and that רבי שמעון holds them liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא recited before רב נחמן: Two who carried out a weaver's reed are exempt, and רבי שמעון holds them liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a version of the same ברייתא that sounds reversed. This sets up רב נחמן's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere, the חכמים make two people liable when neither could carry the item alone, and רבי שמעון exempts them. This version says the opposite, which does not match their known opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter of ברייתות taught before him
Exempt
Holds liable

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ קָנֶה שֶׁל גַּרְדִּי — פְּטוּרִין,
phrases.english: Two who carried out a weaver's reed are exempt,
and Rabbi Shimon holds them liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different version of the ברייתא used in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As recited: חכמים exempt, רבי שמעון obligates.

steps.title: רב נחמן flips the opinions back
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects that the version is backwards and corrects it: they are liable, and רבי שמעון exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which way are you facing?! Rather, say: they are liable, and רבי שמעון exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן objects to the reversed version and fixes the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כלפי לייא' means the reciter turned things the wrong way around. A weaver's reed is too heavy for one person to carry alone (זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול). In that case the known view is that the חכמים hold both liable and רבי שמעון exempts. So the right text is: they are liable, and רבי שמעון exempts. This matches the ברייתא רב אשי quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: Toward which side? An exclamation meaning 'you have it backwards'
Rather, say: introduces a corrected text
Exempts

phrases.english: Which way are you facing?!
Rather say: they are liable,
and Rabbi Shimon exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלַפֵּי לְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the version recited in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חכמים exempt and רבי שמעון obligates
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים obligate and רבי שמעון exempts
steps.whatToRemember: Two people carrying a weaver's reed: חכמים say liable, רבי שמעון says exempt. Whether this shows 'one שיעור for all' was left unproven.

steps.title: The משנה: a vessel or bed is secondary, and the corpse cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that carrying less than a שיעור of food in a vessel is exempt, even for the vessel. Carrying a living person on a bed is exempt, even for the bed. Carrying a corpse on a bed, or the minimum amount of a corpse, נבלה, or שרץ, is liable, while רבי שמעון exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who carries out less than the required amount of food in a vessel is exempt even for the vessel, because the vessel is secondary to the food. One who carries a living person on a bed is exempt even for the bed, because the bed is secondary to him. One who carries a corpse on a bed is liable. Likewise for an olive-bulk of a corpse, an olive-bulk of a נבלה, or a lentil-bulk of a שרץ: he is liable. רבי שמעון exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a container counts as secondary to what it holds, and it lists cases of carrying impure items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel or bed is just a holder, so it does not create its own liability. A living person 'carries himself', so carrying him is exempt, and the bed goes along with him. A corpse cannot carry itself, so carrying it is liable. רבי שמעון exempts in the corpse cases because people carry these things only to get rid of them, which is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Secondary, an accessory to the main thing
Less than the minimum amount
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
A creeping creature that makes things impure in the amount of a lentil
The size of a lentil

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a container is secondary (טפל) to its contents shapes the next ברייתא, about when the vessel itself creates liability.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who carries out foods
less than the measure in a vessel
is exempt even for the vessel,
because the vessel is secondary to it,
a living person on a bed:
exempt even for the bed,
because the bed is secondary to him.
A corpse on a bed: liable,
and likewise an olive-bulk of a corpse
and an olive-bulk of a carcass
and a lentil-bulk of a creeping animal: liable,
and Rabbi Shimon exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצִיא אוֹכָלִין פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר בִּכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; the topic shifts from shared carrying to containers and corpses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A container is secondary to its contents. Carrying a corpse or impure items is liable according to the חכמים and exempt according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: ברייתא: liable for food, and for the vessel too if it was needed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches: carrying a full שיעור of food in a vessel makes one liable for the food but not the vessel. If he needed the vessel for itself, he is liable for the vessel too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One who carries out a full amount of food in a vessel is liable for the food and exempt for the vessel. And if he needed the vessel, he is liable also for the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that covers the case the משנה left out: a full שיעור of food in a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the vessel is just a holder, so there is no liability for it. But if he wanted the vessel for its own sake, carrying it counts on its own, and he is liable for it as well.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs the vessel itself

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
One who carries out foods of the full measure,
if in a vessel, is liable for the food
and exempt for the vessel.
And if the vessel was needed by him,
he is liable also for the vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמּוֹצִיא אוֹכָלִין כְּשִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the משנה in step 18 with the case of a full שיעור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liable for the food only, unless the vessel itself was needed. Then he is liable for both.

steps.title: Does this mean two חטאות for one act?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he is liable for both the food and the vessel, does that mean one who eats two olive-bulks of חלב in one lapse brings two חטאות?
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: one who eats two olive-bulks of forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness is liable for two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא by pointing out a strange result that seems to follow from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying food and vessel together is one act of the same מלאכה in one lapse. Normally that brings only one קרבן חטאת, just as eating two olive-bulks of חלב in one lapse brings only one. So how can there be liability for both the food and the vessel?

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: here it is used to draw out a troubling consequence
Forbidden animal fat
In one lapse of awareness, before he realized he was sinning

steps.confusionAlert: 'חייב' here means liable to bring a קרבן חטאת. The question is whether there is one חטאת or two, not whether the act is forbidden.

phrases.english: Learn from it:
one who eats two olive-bulks of forbidden fat
in one lapse of awareness is liable for two!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, אוֹכֵל שְׁנֵי זֵיתֵי חֵלֶב בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second ruling of the ברייתא in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling 'liable also for the vessel'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One act of one מלאכה in one lapse should bring only one חטאת. The ברייתא seems to require two, like two olive-bulks of חלב eaten together.

steps.title: רב ששת begins to explain the case
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת starts his answer: the ברייתא is dealing with a specific case. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where...
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins to answer by narrowing the case of the ברייתא. The answer continues on the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הכא במאי עסקינן' means the answer will limit the ברייתא to a special situation. In that situation, liability for the vessel does not mean two חטאות for one act.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? Introduces a narrowed case
For example, such as, where

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
With what are we dealing here? Where

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן). It continues on the next amud.
